meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

I'm writing down September 24. A comparison you made in your head isn't a document, so do you have that sample here for me to read? And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. You said version history, Hale, so what does it show, and on which dates? I'm writing down whatever you say.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and an apology to Owen. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with the zero to be withdrawn, and nothing agreed.
What moved her: "taking it off the table" got you a flat okay from her, a small sign of ground, because you gave up the checker on your own.
What cost ground: "I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24" cost you, because you had no sample in hand for her to read, and she had asked twice whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero.
Try next time: when she asks whether anyone spoke to Owen, answer that directly in one sentence, including that the zero went in before you called, and then put the September 24 sample in front of her.
